paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The loss comparison between vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM. SepLLM achieves lower loss different computation costs and different training time consistently.
model_annotation: The plot compares the loss of two models—Vanilla Transformer and SepLLM—as a function of computational cost measured in TFLOPs (terafloating-point operations). The x-axis represents TFLOPs on a linear scale ranging from 0.00 to 1.25 × 10⁹, with tick marks at intervals of 0.25 × 10⁹. The y-axis represents Loss, also on a linear scale, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75, with tick marks at intervals of 0.05. The Vanilla Transformer is depicted by a purple dashed line with triangular markers, starting at approximately 2.74 loss at 0.00 TFLOPs and decreasing gradually to about 2.51 loss at 1.25 × 10⁹ TFLOPs. The SepLLM is shown as a red solid line with circular markers, starting at approximately 2.73 loss at 0.00 TFLOPs and decreasing more steeply to about 2.47 loss at 1.25 × 10⁹ TFLOPs. A green dashed rectangle highlights the region from 1.00 × 10⁹ to 1.25 × 10⁹ TFLOPs, with an annotation indicating a 1.28× improvement in efficiency, suggesting that SepLLM achieves lower loss at comparable or reduced computational cost compared to the Vanilla model.
